title: An AI interface connects users to library collections
summary: Northeastern’s library connected Claude to scholarly collections and reported better discovery in early use; learning gains have not been measured.
source_collection: University of Texas AI Opportunity Inventory
account: Northeastern University Library developed a server and Claude plugin that direct academic requests to library resources and return links to underlying works. Library dean Dan Cohen demonstrated the interface in October 2025. A later account described adding museum collections and retrieving relevant material without ordinary web search. Cohen and Evan Simpson subsequently reported an improved discovery experience in early testing. These are accounts from the deploying institution, without a controlled retrieval benchmark or measured learning outcome.
purpose: The library built an AI interface to help users find scholarly and cultural materials while preserving access to source works.
system: Northeastern University Library MCP server and Claude plugin
segment: Discovery of scholarly and cultural collections
taxonomy_note: The reported result concerns discovery of materials. Learning gains and complete elimination of hallucinations are not established.

ratings.reason: The reviewed sources do not establish the magnitude of the benefit.

ai_role.statement: Claude interpreted requests and used a library server to retrieve materials. Cataloging, collections, access controls, and source links were essential parts of the workflow.
